> `obs_count` is **not comparable across runs** — most fetchers report rows merged this run, thirteen fall back to the whole store when nothing was written. To ask how big this source is, count the store. See ledger R326 and the comment in `updater/state.py`.

> A `partial` NEVER sets `last_success_utc` (R231). A source reading `last SUCCESS: NEVER` may be ingesting millions of rows perfectly well and failing one sub-unit. Check `obs_count` and the run history before concluding it is dead.

> **A FUTURE `last_obs_date` IS USUALLY CORRECT, NOT A BUG.** Many publishers ship genuine PROJECTIONS: CSO Ireland's `18_Population_Projections` runs to 2057, Estonia's `rahvastik` to 2085, ABS to 2046/2071, UN WPP to 2101, IMF WEO to 2031. `health.py` already separates the two — `frontier` is the furthest period held INCLUDING projections (display only), `newest_obs` filters to periods <= today and is the recency signal — because 28 of 93 units legitimately reported a future frontier. Do NOT "repair" a future date until you have looked at the series key and the year sequence.
>
> What IS a defect: a SENTINEL (9999-12-31, 2999-12-31) or a COUNTER read as a year (years 1, 2, 3 ... contiguous from 1 — no projection starts at year 1). Tell them apart by the key and the sequence, never by the size of the number. See R320/R322 and `tools/audit_impossible_dates.py`, whose bounds (before 1500, after 2200) are deliberately far outside every real projection horizon.

## 3. How it works

**Why this strategy** (registry `strategy_reason`):

> CSO PxStat ReadDataset returns whole tables with NO startPeriod param (so not SDMX-delta-able), but the Navigation.Search catalog carries per-table release-date metadata — gate on that release date and overwrite only changed tables/subjects.

**Adapter contract** (registry `adapter`):

- `vintage_signal`: Refresh _catalog.json each run via PxStat Navigation.Search and compare each table's release/last-modified field (e.g. RlsLiveDatetimeFrom / RlsArchiveFlag) against the stored value; re-pull and overwrite only tables whose release date moved.
- `since_param`: n/a (ReadDataset has no startPeriod; whole-table re-pull on change, no server-side date filter)
- `out_paths_note`: MULTIPLE files: ~46 per-subject-group parquets keyed by SbjCode (e.g. 26_Labour_Market.parquet, 29_National_Accounts.parquet) + cached _catalog.json. A changed table maps into its owning subject parquet — must read-existing + append + dedup on (key,date) rather than skip whole subject.
- `rate_note`: no key (ws.cso.ie JSON-RPC + REST); self-throttle RATE=0.4s; 429 handled with 30s sleep; stale cached _catalog.json silently freezes the table universe — must refresh it each run.

**Fetcher module**: [`updater/strategies/fetchers/cso.py`](../../updater/strategies/fetchers/cso.py)

<details><summary>Its own module docstring — the authoritative description, including every defect previously found and why the code looks the way it does</summary>

```
S1 fetcher — CSO Ireland (Central Statistics Office, PxStat).

License CC BY 4.0, no key (ws.cso.ie JSON-RPC + REST). The data lives in ~44+ per-
subject grouped parquets under clean_full/cso/<SbjCode>_<SbjValue>.parquet, each with
schema (series_key, obs_date, value) and series_key = "CSO:<MtrCode>:<dim>=<code>:...".
A table revision lands in its owning subject parquet, so we read-existing + append +
dedup on (series_key, obs_date) per subject (NEVER skip a whole subject).

PxStat's ReadDataset has NO startPeriod param, so we can't do an SDMX-style server-side
date delta — we re-pull WHOLE changed tables. Change detection is the PxStat collection's
per-table `updated` release datetime: `PxStat.Data.Cube_API.ReadCollection` returns a
JSON-stat collection of every dataset carrying {extension.matrix -> updated}. We gate on
that: re-pull + overwrite only matrices whose `updated` moved vs. the stored cursor.

  current_vintage(unit): cheap-ish probe — ReadCollection restricted to a recent window
      (trailing ~120d via the `datefrom` param) returns only RECENTLY-revised tables (a few
      MB, ~1-2k matrices vs. the full 22MB/12.7k). Hash the {matrix: updated} map of that
      window: it changes iff any table was revised recently. None if it can't be fetched.
  update(unit, since): full ReadCollection {matrix: updated}; diff against stored
      _collupd.json; re-fetch only NEW/CHANGED matrices (newest-revision-first, bounded by
      MAX_TABLES per run so a run stays finite and converges across ticks); route each into
      its owning subject parquet (from the cached _catalog.json) and merge.merge_and_write
      (mode='merge', dedup (series_key,obs_date)). Persist the release-date cursor only for
      matrices actually pulled, so a transient mid-run failure re-pulls next tick.
```

</details>

**Ingest script(s)**: `jobs/ingest_cso_ireland.py`

## 4. If it stops updating — diagnose in this order

Run everything from `E:\research\econfindatalibrary`.

```bash
# 1. What does the system actually say? (not what you remember)
python -c "import sys,sqlite3;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config;con=sqlite3.connect(f'file:{config.STATE_DB}?mode=ro',uri=True);print(*con.execute(\"SELECT unit_id,status,last_success_utc,last_attempt_utc,last_error FROM unit_state WHERE source_id='cso'\"),sep=chr(10))"

# 2. Is it even being ATTEMPTED? 'scheduled' is not 'attempted' (R246).
#    A daily run reaches ~20 of ~106 cloud sources; most are skipped on cadence, which is normal.
python -m updater.run --source cso --dry

# 3. Run it for real and READ THE REASON. Failures name themselves now.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -u -m updater.run --source cso --force

# 4. Is the PUBLISHER healthy, or is it us? Probe upstream directly, never a relay.
#    (DBnomics is BANNED — every source must be reached at its own publisher.)

# 5. Is the store intact? obs_count in state is NOT the answer.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -c "import sys,os;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config,blob;d=config.source_dir('cso');fs=[f for f in blob.list_parquets(d) if not os.path.basename(f).startswith('_')];print(len(fs),'files',sum(blob.row_count(os.path.join(d,os.path.basename(f))) for f in fs),'rows')"

# 6. Are its dates real? A counter-as-year or a 9999 sentinel is silent (7 sources hit).
#    NOTE: a FUTURE date is usually a legitimate projection - check the key before repairing.
python tools/audit_impossible_dates.py --r2 --source cso
```

**Read the failure class before fixing anything.** From the 2026-08-04 audit of every unfetchable source, the causes were: `budget_deferral` (NOT broken — ran out of its time slice), `code_bug`, `rate_limited`, `gated_by_design`. **Zero** were an expired credential or a dead endpoint, although that is the usual first guess.

If the error names sub-units as `deferred (budget N min)` or `budget spent`, **nothing has failed** — the source ran out of its slice and the rest is taken next tick (R303). Do not 'fix' it.

## 4b. Root cause when this was last investigated (2026-08-04)

*From the unfetchable-source audit — 29 agents, every finding challenged by a skeptic before it was accepted. This source was covered by the target `cso`.*

- **root cause**: `code_bug`  (confidence high)
- **which units**: 36 of 46 sub-units transient-failed in CI run 30796923747 (cso/_all, 2026-08-03T09:25-09:26Z, 113s). The brief's premise is CONFIRMED but over-attributed: only 27 of the 36 carry the "no subject mapping in catalog" label; the other 9 are a separate, already-named parse/no-body class that DID print to the log (EDA21, MTD05, MTD06, MTD07, MTD08, MTH05, MTH06, MTH07, MTH08). Reconstructing the run's batch from the live ReadCollection map plus the R2 cursor reproduces both halves exactly: batch = changed[:60] contains exactly 27 matrices absent from the cached catalog and exactly those 9 named matrices -> 27 + 9 = 36. The remaining 24 of the 60 were pulled successfully; the other 10 tally units are subject-parquet publishes.
- **blast radius**: 222 of the 12,908 currently-live CSO matrices (1.72%) have no entry in the cached _catalog.json, so they can never be routed to an owning subject parquet and are never ingested. Because an unmapped matrix never enters pulled_ok, its release-date cursor never advances (cso.py:369-372), so it re-enters `changed` on every single tick - permanently. `changed` is sorted newest-revision-first, and new tables are by definition newest, so the unmapped set crowds out real work: 27 of the 60 MAX_TABLES slots (45%) in the reconstructed batch are matrices guaranteed to fail again. The source therefore cannot converge over its ~44 subject parquets / 48.9M-row store. The cache's effective as-of date is before 2026-06-11: the 222 unmapped matrices' live RlsLiveDatetimeFrom values span 2026-06-11T11:00:00 to 2026-07-31T11:12:54.53 (73 released in June, 149 in July). It also holds 678 codes no longer present in ReadCollection.
- fixable by us: **True**

**Recommended fix, in order:**

> Two one-line-class fixes, both on our side; no publisher contact and no credential needed.
> 
> 1. Refresh-on-miss in updater/strategies/fetchers/cso.py `_matrix_subject_map()` (lines 111-141): after computing `batch`, if ANY matrix in it is absent from the map, re-fetch the Search catalog from ws.cso.ie ONCE per run, rewrite the cache via blob.write_bytes_atomic, and re-look-up before failing. Add an age bound (e.g. rebuild if the cached object is older than 7 days) so the cache cannot silently freeze again. One extra 14 MB request per run at most, and only when a miss actually occurs.
> 
> 2. Make jobs/ingest_cso_ireland.py `build_catalog()` bypassable (line 83): add a `force`/`refresh` parameter so `if os.path.exists(CATALOG_FILE)` can be skipped. Without this, fix 1's fallback still cannot reach the network on the workstation, and the same stale bytes keep being re-uploaded to R2.
> 
> 3. Add a `print(f"[cso] {mtr}: no subject mapping in catalog")` to the branch at cso.py:281-285. It is the only failure branch that names itself in the tally but writes nothing to the log - the reason 27 of 36 failures were invisible in CI while the other 9 were diagnosable at a glance.
> 
> After the fix, the 222 currently-unroutable matrices become fetchable (verified: SIH13 and SIA208 both return outcome='ok' today) and stop consuming 45% of every run's 60-table budget, which is what has been preventing convergence.
> 
> Out of scope but observed in the same run and worth a separate ticket: `last_obs=5630-12-31` and `[merge] IMPOSSIBLE DATES: 6,000 of 70,581 row(s) ... 5_Services.parquet are dated after 2200 - e.g. CSO:RSA03:TLIST(A1)=2005:STATISTIC=RSA03C1 -> 4711-12-31` (a swapped time axis), plus the 9 EDA21/MTD*/MTH* no-row matrices, which are a distinct parser-grammar defect, not this one.

## 6. Rules that apply to every repair here

- **A key/parser change is a RE-PULL, never a merge** (R22). Changing what `series_key` means leaves the old and new grains coexisting; dedup cannot collapse them because they no longer collide. Use `mode="replace"`, or re-pull the table.
- **Never patch dates — re-pull** (R288). A naive date repair on `cso` would have destroyed 11 of 12 rows; only a negative control caught it. And 41,091 of `stat_slovenia`'s fabricated dates land in 1900–2200, indistinguishable from real data, so no date test can find them.
- **Verify against the store you are actually serving** (R296/R36). Under `AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2` the local directory is a scratch mirror of the last run only; a local check can under-report or give the opposite answer.
- **When a probe reports ABSENCE, run it against something known PRESENT** (R316). An absence looks identical whether the data is missing or the probe is broken.
- **Compare (key, date) pairs, not just keys** (R314). A re-key check that compares identifiers verifies the half you changed on purpose; the half you changed by accident is in the values.
- **A bound over a fixed order is a truncation, not a budget** (R190). If work is capped, check it ROTATES — and specifically that it rotates when the item at the head never completes (R313).
- **Read the job's ARGV, not its progress** (R323). A `--dry-run` and a real run print the same numbers.
